acceptance: The SSB generator draws all random values from a per-instance random.Random seeded in the generator, never from the global random module

Generated SSB data is byte-identical to today's output at SF 0.01 and 0.1, or, if the stream necessarily changes, ssb_results.py, the corpus and the integration pin in tests/integration/test_ssb_cross_surface_equivalence.py are updated together with the reason stated
A test shows that global random calls, or a second generator built before generation, no longer change the generated files
SSB SQL and DataFrame runs at SF 0.01 and 0.1 still validate as passed
context: Implemented in PR #3113 (branch fix/ssb-generator-deterministic-rng, commit bd590753a): per-instance random.Random(42), byte-identical SF0.01 output verified, regression test fails on old code, 33 targeted tests pass. PR armed 2026-10-18; after merge, take and finish this item.
description:
SSBDataGenerator seeds the process-wide RNG once, in its constructor (benchbox/core/ssb/generator.py:51 `random.seed(42)`). All row generation then draws from the global `random` module (generator.py:11 `import random`; for example :341, :343, :378, :510-513, :548-560). The generated data therefore depends on every other use of `random` in the process between construction and generation, and on the order generators are built. Examples: two generators built before either runs, a library or test that draws a random number, or generating with one instance twice.

This now matters for correctness. PR #3065 (commit 87adc2cd9) added exact per-query SSB row counts (benchbox/core/expected_results/ssb_results.py), and DataFrame validation fails a run whose counts differ. Data drawn from a disturbed RNG gives wrong counts and a FAILED run, not a benchmark defect.

How found: while checking during #3065 that the SSB counts are stable. Reproduced on origin/develop 27f7a7d1f: generating `customer` at SF 0.01 normally gives md5 434197e8; building a second generator and calling `random.random()` once before generate_data gives 6e492a9c. Normal CLI runs are not affected today, because construction and generation happen back to back with no other random use. Fresh runs on 2026-10-16 matched the corpus counts from August.
